name: Do I need permits for a kitchen remodel in Los Angeles?

mainEntity.name: Do I need permits for a kitchen remodel in Los Angeles if I am not moving walls?
mainEntity.text: Do I need permits for a kitchen remodel in Los Angeles if I am not moving walls?

acceptedAnswer.text: Whether permits are needed depends on the actual scope of work, not just whether the walls stay put. In Los Angeles, a cosmetic update such as painting, replacing cabinet doors, or swapping fixtures may not require a permit. But the moment the project includes new circuits, outlet changes, plumbing moves, gas line changes, HVAC changes, or any structural modification, permit review and inspections usually become part of the process. Even when the layout remains the same, many full kitchen remodels still trigger permit requirements because hidden trade work is involved. Homeowners should verify permit responsibility before signing a contract and confirm who handles plan check, scheduling inspections, and correction notices. Skipping permits can create resale issues, insurance problems, and delays if work has to be reopened later.
acceptedAnswer.description: Permits are often required when a kitchen remodel involves electrical, plumbing, gas, structural, or ventilation changes, even if the walls stay in place. Simple cosmetic work may not need a permit, but most full remodels in Los Angeles do because they usually involve regulated trades and inspections.
